key_insight: Symmetry-preserving variational circuits accurately approximate lattice Gross–Neveu states, while transferred adaptive circuits extend one-flavor simulations to 400 qubits.
engineering_relevance: At fixed flavor count, range caps, and append count, the adaptive design has a precompilation local-factor count linear in volume and a volume-independent shared-parameter count.
method: Build fixed circuits conserving total fermion number or each flavor number.
Use SC-ADAPT-VQE with bulk, boundary-sensitive, and cross-flavor generators.
Prepare sector-resolved excited states through sequential deflation.
evidence_signal: Classical benchmarks reach 30 qubits; selected massive fixed circuits achieve relative energy errors of approximately 10⁻⁵–2×10⁻⁴, while one-flavor circuit transfers to 60–400 qubits show 0.35%–1.76% deviations from DMRG references.
watch_item: Fixed-accuracy scaling to arbitrary volumes remains unestablished, and the reported evaluations are classical simulations rather than quantum-hardware demonstrations.
paper_title: Symmetry-Preserving and Scalable Variational Circuits for the Lattice Gross-Neveu Model
